title: Decision 0008: signalman is a tool for agents, not an agent
description:
Write docs/decisions/0008-signalman-is-a-tool-for-agents.md from the template, status accepted, and link it from docs/decisions/README.md, docs/architecture.md and docs/roadmap.md.

Context: the Cersei evaluation recorded on the parent epic (signalman-4gp), and the recurring question "should signalman investigate or remediate on its own".

Considered options: (1) embed an agentic loop (Cersei or similar) inside the triage path; (2) expose signalman's typed capabilities to external agents over MCP and a stable JSON contract, with no generative model in the binary; (3) do nothing.

Outcome: option 2. Consequences: the deterministic core and decisions 0001 and 0002 hold; a generative model may appear only in offline tooling outside the triage path and never writes to incident.io; every capability an agent can call is one signalman already exposes in the CLI.

Confirmation: Cargo.toml carries no LLM SDK dependency; the MCP tool list is generated from the same code paths as the CLI subcommands; a test asserts the write tool is absent when mcp.allow_write is false.

Revisit criteria, stated in the record: a responder need that cannot be decomposed into deterministic retrieval plus a typed question; live verification (signalman-b11) complete; a human approval channel in incident.io (workflow or decision flow) that signalman can wait on.
acceptance_criteria: ADR 0008 merged with frontmatter, linked from the decisions index, architecture and roadmap; CLAUDE.md rule added: no generative-model SDK in the triage path, agents call signalman over MCP.
close_reason: ADR 0008 written, linked from the decisions index, architecture, roadmap, mkdocs nav; CLAUDE.md rule added.

title: Change feed adapters: Argo CD and GitLab webhooks in their native shapes
description:
The change feed (decision 0007) takes signalman's own JSON, which asks every pipeline to write a template. Two sources cover most deploys here and both can post their native payload: Argo CD notifications can send the Application object ({{ toJson .app }}), and GitLab project webhooks send documented event payloads with X-Gitlab-Event and X-Gitlab-Token headers.

Add two adapter endpoints that translate into Change and record it:
- POST /changes/argocd: an Argo CD Application (or {app, context}); component = metadata.name; kind deploy; summary from the last history entry or operationState (revision, destination namespace, images, initiator); at = history.deployedAt or operationState.finishedAt; url = context.argocdUrl/applications/<name> when the context is posted. Bearer token as the plain feed.
- POST /changes/gitlab: X-Gitlab-Token compared in constant time against the feed token; X-Gitlab-Event decides the mapping: Deployment Hook (status success only) -> deploy; Feature Flag Hook -> flag; Release Hook -> release; Merge Request Hook (action merge) -> merge. Other events answer 200 ignored. component = project.name lowercased.

Wire types lenient (unknown fields ignored). Fixtures from the official docs under examples/changes/. Tests per adapter plus router tests. docs/changes.md documents both setups; the generic endpoint stays.
close_reason: POST /changes/argocd (Application object, bearer) and POST /changes/gitlab (X-Gitlab-Token, X-Gitlab-Event: Deployment success, Feature Flag, Release create, Merge Request merge) translate native payloads into changes; failed syncs and non-change events answer 200 ignored; fixtures from the documented payloads under examples/changes; unit and router tests; docs/changes.md documents both setups.

title: Collect labelled alert history for the harness
description: The harness (signalman eval) is only as good as its cases. Export resolved alerts from incident.io (GET /v2/alerts with created_at[gte] over the last quarter, plus the incident each was attached to and its final severity) and derive labels: owner = the team of the responder or the incident lead, impact = the incident's closing severity mapped to none/minor/major/outage, actionable = whether an incident was declared or the alert was acknowledged, duplicate_of = the incident the alert was merged into, action = what the on-call actually did. Target at least 50 cases per question so the calibration bins are populated. Store under examples/eval/ only if free of customer data; otherwise keep the file out of the repository.

title: Layered configuration: file, environment, command line
description:
The binary is configured by environment variables and a few flags, read in six different places. That works for one laptop and breaks in Kubernetes, where shape (URLs, thresholds, rubric text, team list) belongs in a ConfigMap under review, secrets belong in a Secret, and an operator needs to know which value won.

Deliver one configuration model with an explicit precedence, lowest to highest: built-in default, configuration file (TOML), environment variable, command-line flag. Every environment read moves into one module so the precedence table in the docs is the code. Secrets (API keys, tokens, webhook secret) are never accepted from the file.

Also move what was compiled but is really configuration into the file: policy thresholds, the fallback team list, the impact rubric, and the text of every question. The set of questions and their types stay in code: the policy consumes them and the typed handles exist to keep that contract honest.
close_reason: All children delivered; follow-ups are ordinary settings additions through the documented three-place rule.

title: Decision 0005: observability signals enter through incident.io, no direct Tsuga client
description: Record the Tsuga assessment as a MADR decision. Evidence: Tsuga's OpenAPI spec exists at GET https://api.tsuga.com/v0/open-api (and /v0/internal-open-api) but answers 401 without an operation API key; nothing public documents it. The web app's bundles show POST /v0/alerts/ongoing/query with filters (owners, searchQuery, priorities, clusterIds, triggeredBy key:value dimensions, types monitor|slo) sorted by priority; a service catalog under /v0/service-catalog; and a native incident.io notification integration. Options weighed: direct Tsuga client from the reverse-engineered contract; Tsuga alerts forwarded into incident.io by Tsuga's own integration and read back through GET /v2/alerts; both. Chosen: through incident.io, consistent with decision 0001. Revisit when an operation API key allows reading the spec (deferred child).

title: Related firing alerts as blast-radius context
description:
An alert is qualified faster when the responder and the model see what else is firing. Fetch firing alerts created within a window (GET /v2/alerts?status[one_of]=firing&created_at[gte]=<now-window>, page_size 50), exclude the alert itself, cap the list (20), and add them to the state as alert.related_alerts with title, age in minutes and the component label when present. Reference the path in the impact question guidance (several alerts on the same component or its dependents indicate broader impact) and in the dedup question. List them in the qualification note.

Observability alerts from Tsuga reach this list through Tsuga's native incident.io notification integration; no Tsuga client is added (decision 0005).

Acceptance: state contains related_alerts in the wiremock e2e test; window configurable with SIGNALMAN_RELATED_WINDOW_MINUTES (default 30); a failure to list related alerts degrades to an empty list with a warning.
close_reason: Implemented on claude/rust-typesafe-api-zf13d9: note.rs, related alerts in sync.rs, time_to_qualify, decision 0005, docs

title: Qualification note on the incident.io alert
description:
Tags encode the verdict but not the reasoning, the confidence, or where to look next. A responder still opens Backstage, the runbook and the incident list by hand. Post one markdown note on the alert (POST /v1/alert_notes, alert_id) that carries everything the tags imply plus what they cannot: owner with confidence and the confirm-owner flag, impact level with its distribution, actionable probability, the matched incident with permalink, suspected change, the resolved catalog component and owner group as Backstage links, the TechDocs runbook page link, the upstream alert link, related firing alerts, and the time to qualify.

Rules: deterministic template in code (decision 0002: no generated text). Exactly one signalman note per alert: list existing notes (GET /v1/alert_notes?alert_id=) and PUT the existing one when its first line carries the signalman marker, so retriage rewrites in place instead of stacking. Respect WriteBack::DryRun. A note failure is logged and must not undo tags or attachments. Backstage links need BACKSTAGE_APP_URL (frontend), defaulting to BACKSTAGE_BASE_URL.

Acceptance: wiremock test asserts the note body and the create-or-replace behaviour; Outcome gains note_id; docs updated (incident.io page, configuration).
close_reason: Implemented on claude/rust-typesafe-api-zf13d9: note.rs, related alerts in sync.rs, time_to_qualify, decision 0005, docs

title: Reduce mean time to qualify (MTTQ)
description:
Mean time to qualify: the time from an alert being created in incident.io to the moment a responder has, in one place, the answers to five questions: is it actionable, who owns it, how bad is it, is it already a known incident, and did something change. signalman already computes those judgments; the gap is that they surface only as tags, without the reasoning, the links or the surrounding context, and that nobody measures the interval.

Scope, deliberately small (Unix rule: few things, done well):
1. One qualification note on the alert in incident.io, rewritten in place, with judgments, links (incident, Backstage component and owner group, TechDocs runbook, upstream alert) and the time to qualify.
2. Other firing alerts in the window as blast-radius context, in the model state and in the note.
3. Time to qualify measured per alert (alert created_at to decision) in the outcome, logs and note.
4. Decision record: observability signals (Tsuga) enter through incident.io; no direct Tsuga client until the spec is verified with an operation API key.

Out of scope, recorded as deferred children: on-call lookup through incident.io schedules; a direct Tsuga client.

title: MCP server: expose qualification, related alerts, recent changes and ownership as read-only tools
description:
Let the agents responders already use call signalman's typed judgments. A new subcommand `signalman mcp` serves the Model Context Protocol over stdio (Streamable HTTP later, mounted on the existing axum router when a bearer token is configured). Use the official Rust SDK, rmcp (modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk, 3.x), with only the server and stdio transport features; no other new dependency.

Tools, all read-only, each a thin wrapper over the code the CLI subcommand already calls so there is exactly one implementation per capability:
- qualify_alert(alert_id | alert JSON): full triage in dry-run mode; returns the Outcome contract (schema v1) with every probability, the decision and the links. Writes nothing.
- related_alerts(alert_id | component, window_minutes): the blast-radius list the flow computes.
- recent_changes(component?, window_minutes): matches from the in-process ChangeLog (empty when the feed is not configured, with a reason).
- lookup_owner(component | alert text): Backstage resolution, candidates and the runbook page.
- open_incidents(): the dedup candidate list.
Each tool has an input schema from schemars, a one-paragraph description written for a model (what it answers, what it never does), and returns structured content plus a short text fallback.

Rules carried over: never creates incidents (decision 0001); no generative model anywhere (decisions 0002 and 0008); secrets stay env-only; configuration under a new [mcp] table (enabled, transport, bind address) with rows in docs/configuration.md and env vars in ENV_VARS.

Observability: one tracing span per tool call carrying the tool name, duration and whether it failed, so signalman-m28.2 exports it with the rest.

Docs: docs/mcp.md with a Claude Code `.mcp.json` example and an incident.io assistant note; mkdocs nav; README feature line.
acceptance_criteria: signalman mcp lists the five tools over stdio; an in-process rmcp client test calls qualify_alert against wiremock TypeSafe and incident.io mocks and receives an Outcome that validates against docs/schema/outcome.v1.json; a test asserts no write happens in qualify_alert; configuration table and docs page; contract-reviewer pass on the incident.io and Backstage boundaries.

Streamable HTTP split out to signalman-4gp.7.

title: Runbook section suggestion as a typed Choice in the qualification note
description:
The investigation people expect from an "agent" on an alert is mostly: open the runbook, find the step that matches this failure. signalman already retrieves the runbook excerpt from TechDocs (src/backstage/enrich.rs, alert.runbook, one page capped at 1,800 characters) and puts it in the state. Deliver the step selection as a typed question, no agent loop.

Design:
- Split the excerpt deterministically on Markdown headings into sections; keep heading, anchor and the first sentence. Sections are options for a Choice question "Which runbook section applies to this alert" with a no-match option, referencing `alert.runbook_sections` by path. Ask only when there are at least two sections (the model cannot choose what is not offered).
- Policy: surface the chosen section only above a confidence threshold in Policy (default conservative); below it the note says no section matched.
- Note: one line under the runbook link: the section title as a deep link (TechDocs anchor), with its probability. Fixed template, no prose from the model.
- Outcome: `runbook_section` in the JSON contract (signalman-4gp child "Stable JSON contract").
- Eval: add expected.runbook_section to the case format as optional; grade it when present.

Load the typesafe:typesafe-ai skill and use the question-designer agent before writing the question. Live TechDocs verification (signalman-b11.5) should run before trusting the section split on a real backend.
acceptance_criteria: Choice question with no-match option asked only when two or more sections exist; threshold in Policy and documented in docs/configuration.md; note line with deep link; field in outcome schema; wiremock test with a multi-section runbook; harness grades the field when present.

title: Stable JSON contract for the triage outcome (schema v1)
description:
Agents and scripts drive signalman through `triage --json`, `incidentio triage-alert --json` and the eval report, but the shape is whatever serde emits from Outcome today: field names follow the Rust struct and a rename is silently breaking. Make the outcome a contract.

Scope:
- An `Outcome` wire type with `schema_version: 1`, stable snake_case names, every optional field present as null, probabilities as numbers in [0,1], the decision as an enum string, related alerts and recent changes as arrays of typed objects, links as URLs, and time_to_qualify_seconds.
- Emit it from every `--json` path and from the webhook outcome log line, so the CLI, the server log and the future MCP server share one shape.
- Generate the JSON Schema with schemars into docs/schema/outcome.v1.json and a test that fails when the emitted shape drifts from the committed schema.
- Document it in docs/triage.md (or a new docs/contract.md) with one full example.

Non-goals: no change to the qualification note template; no change to the TypeSafe request shape.
acceptance_criteria: schemars-derived docs/schema/outcome.v1.json committed; a test round-trips the example alerts through triage --json and validates against the schema; docs page with the example; existing tests updated, no field silently renamed.
close_reason: src/outcome.rs wire contract v1, both emitters, schema outcome subcommand, mise run schema, docs/schema/outcome.v1.json, 13 contract tests incl. drift, validation, round-trip and CLI end-to-end; docs/triage.md section with validated example.

title: Agent interoperability: signalman as a tool for agents, not an agent
description:
Cersei (github.com/pacifio/cersei, crates.io 0.2.6, MIT) was evaluated on 2026-09-22 as a way to give signalman agent capabilities. It is a Rust SDK for coding agents: a generative-LLM agentic loop (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Vertex) that decides which tools to call, plus sub-agents, file/shell/web tools, memory tiers, skills, an MCP client and a serialisable workflow engine.

Not adopted, for three reasons.

1. Thesis mismatch. Decision 0002 says no model generates text anywhere in signalman: deterministic logic in code, the model answers narrow typed questions. An agentic loop is the opposite: the model chooses actions and writes prose. Decision 0001 bounds writes to incident.io to tags, attachments and one note. An agent with tools inside the triage path would need both decisions reopened.

2. Weight. cersei-tools pulls five tree-sitter grammars, tantivy, nix, an LSP client and an embeddings crate; cersei-agent pulls memory, MCP and compression; the whole tree uses reqwest 0.12 and chrono where signalman uses reqwest 0.13 and jiff, so the binary would carry two HTTP stacks. signalman has about sixteen direct dependencies today.

3. Maturity. Single maintainer, 0.2.x with in-code notes of removed APIs, 700 crates.io downloads, no MSRV. Its abstractions (working directory, session, CLAUDE.md memory) are shaped for a coding CLI, not a service.

What responders and their tooling actually need is the inverse: signalman's typed judgments callable from agents they already use (Claude Code, Claude in Slack, incident.io's own assistant, internal copilots). That keeps the deterministic core and makes signalman a building block. Children, in order: a decision record; a stable JSON contract for the outcome; a read-only MCP server over the existing capabilities; an opt-in write tool; llms.txt for the docs; and a deferred record for agent-driven remediation so the question is not reopened without its criteria.

The one place agent-style investigation adds MTTQ value, choosing the runbook section that applies, is delivered as a typed question under signalman-3l7 instead.

title: Streamable HTTP transport for the MCP server, mounted on the serve router
description:
signalman-4gp.5 shipped stdio only, by design (the bead capped scope to "server and stdio transport features; no other new dependency"). mcp.transport = "http" is already accepted in configuration and fails clearly at start-up naming this bead.

Scope: mount signalman::mcp::Server (already transport-agnostic: it takes any AsyncRead + AsyncWrite pair rmcp's transport-io feature exposes) on the axum router serve already runs, using rmcp's server-side HTTP transport feature (server-side-http, Streamable HTTP per the MCP spec) instead of a hand-rolled endpoint. Bind address from mcp.bind_address; if unset, mount on the same address and router as the webhook receiver (a new path, e.g. /mcp) rather than opening a second listener, so one process has one place to be reached.

Auth: a bearer token, the same shape as SIGNALMAN_CHANGES_TOKEN (env-only secret, decision 0006), checked before the MCP request reaches rmcp's handler. Do not reuse the webhook signing secret (different trust boundary: a webhook is incident.io authenticating to us, this is an agent authenticating to us).

The one thing HTTP mode changes in practice: recent_changes is no longer always-empty, since the same process now can (if also running serve, or if a future change lets the MCP-only process host /changes too) share a ChangeLog with a live feed. Decide and document whether signalman mcp --transport http implies serve's routes are mounted too, or stays MCP-only with its own /changes.

Non-goals: no new tools, no write tool (that is signalman-4gp.6), no change to the stdio path.
acceptance_criteria: signalman mcp with mcp.transport = "http" (or a combined serve+mcp mode, decided during implementation) serves MCP over Streamable HTTP on mcp.bind_address; a bearer token is required and documented; a wiremock-free integration test drives a tool call over real HTTP; docs/mcp.md and docs/configuration.md updated.
close_reason: Streamable HTTP transport shipped: src/mcp/http.rs mounts rmcp's StreamableHttpService at /mcp, stateless (no session id, JSON responses), behind SIGNALMAN_MCP_TOKEN checked in front of rmcp. serve mounts it on its own listener when the token is set and shares the change feed with recent_changes; signalman mcp with transport=http serves MCP alone on mcp.bind_address. New setting mcp.allowed_hosts. tests/mcp_http.rs drives initialize, tools/list and recent_changes over real HTTP with an rmcp client, proves 401 for no/wrong/feed token, the shared feed on the serve router and the host check; smoke-tested the real binary with curl. docs/mcp.md (Transports), configuration.md, operations.md, roadmap.md, architecture.md, README, CLAUDE.md, .env.example, examples/config updated.

title: MCP write tool apply_qualification behind mcp.allow_write (default off)
description:
Once an agent has seen a qualify_alert result and a human has agreed, let it ask signalman to apply that exact result: tags, the qualification note rewritten in place, and the incident attachment when the decision says so. This is the same write path the webhook flow uses; the tool adds nothing the flow cannot already do and never creates an incident (decision 0001).

Design:
- Input is the Outcome the agent received (schema v1) plus the alert id, not free parameters: signalman re-derives the writes from the typed answers, so the agent cannot invent a tag or a note line.
- Guard: the tool is registered only when mcp.allow_write is true (file or SIGNALMAN_MCP_ALLOW_WRITE); a test asserts it is absent otherwise. Note text stays the fixed template; the agent's name and the MCP client id are recorded in the outcome log, never in the note.
- Idempotent: applying the same Outcome twice is a no-op on tags and replaces the note in place.
- Streamable HTTP transport, if enabled, requires the bearer token; stdio is trusted by the process boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Tool present only when mcp.allow_write is true; wiremock test shows tags, one note (replaced in place on the second call) and the attachment; never calls POST /v1/incidents; configuration row and docs section.
close_reason: apply_qualification write tool shipped: registered only when mcp.allow_write is true (default off, SIGNALMAN_MCP_ALLOW_WRITE), re-derives every write (tags, note, attachment) from the caller's Outcome document via validate()/decision()/answers()/expected_tags(), never creates an incident. 16 wiremock tests in tests/mcp_server.rs cover the page and attach-to-incident paths, alert_id mismatch rejection, tool absence/presence gated on allow_write, and idempotent replace-in-place on a second call. docs/mcp.md, docs/configuration.md and docs/roadmap.md updated; CLAUDE.md's Agents rule reworded now that the write tool exists.

title: Publish llms.txt for the documentation site

The three contracts signalman depends on all publish llms.txt (TypeSafe, incident.io, Backstage docs), and CLAUDE.md tells agents to start there. signalman's own docs should offer the same entry point so an agent asked to operate or extend signalman reads the right pages in the right order.

Generate docs/llms.txt at build time from mkdocs.yml nav (a tiny script under scripts/ or a mise task, not a hand-maintained file): one line per page with title and description from the frontmatter, ordered as the nav is. Add an llms-full.txt concatenation only if the site stays under a few hundred kilobytes. Link it from docs/index.md and the README documentation table. Check the generated file in the docs gate (mise run check) so it cannot drift from the nav.
acceptance_criteria: docs/llms.txt generated from mkdocs.yml frontmatter; a check task fails when it is stale; linked from index and README.
close_reason: docs/llms.txt and docs/llms-full.txt (llmstxt.org) generated by scripts/gen-llms-txt.sh (POSIX sh+awk, no new toolchain) from the mkdocs.yml nav and page frontmatter: nav order, top-level pages then each nav group as a section, raw-Markdown links on main derived from repo_url; a page opts out with llms: false (only the ADR template). --check mode regenerates to a temp dir and fails on drift, also when a docs/ page is missing from the nav; wired into mise docs:check (so mise run check), CI, and a prek hook; mise run docs:llms rewrites. title: Agent-driven remediation: deferred until its criteria are met
description:
Recorded so the question is not reopened from scratch. Executing runbook steps (rollbacks, restarts, scaling) from signalman, whether by an embedded agent SDK such as Cersei or by a hand-written loop, is out of scope until all of the following hold:

1. Decision 0008 is revisited with a responder need that cannot be met by deterministic retrieval plus a typed question plus an external agent calling signalman over MCP.
2. Live verification (signalman-b11) is complete and the harness (signalman eval) shows the qualification decisions are calibrated on real history (signalman-ufg.6), because remediation compounds every qualification error.
3. A human approval channel exists in incident.io that signalman can wait on (a workflow or decision flow), with the approver, the action and the target written to the incident timeline before anything runs.
4. The action surface is an allow-list of idempotent operations with a dry-run mode, each with its own permission, audit event and OpenTelemetry span (signalman-m28.2).

When reopened, re-evaluate the SDK choice at that time; Cersei's Tool, PermissionPolicy and Hook traits are a reasonable shape for an allow-listed action surface, but its dependency weight and maturity were disqualifying in 2026-09.

value: Architecture rule (decision signalman-p2w, docs/decisions/0001): incident.io stays the alert hub. signalman only writes alert tags (ai-team-*, ai-impact-*, ai-action-*, ai-dup-*, ai-suspected-change), POST /v2/incident_alerts attachments, and one qualification note per alert (/v1/alert_notes, marker line '**Signalman qualification**', replaced in place on retriage), or feeds an HTTP alert source with judgments under metadata.ai. Never create incidents directly; alert routes own that.

Cersei (pacifio/cersei, Rust coding-agent SDK, 0.2.6) evaluated 2026-09-22 and not adopted: agentic loop contradicts decisions 0001/0002, heavy tree (tree-sitter x5, tantivy, reqwest 0.12 vs our 0.13), single maintainer, 700 downloads, no MCP server (client only). Direction instead: signalman is a tool for agents, epic signalman-4gp (ADR 0008, Outcome JSON contract v1, rmcp MCP server read-only then gated write, llms.txt). Runbook-section Choice under signalman-3l7.8. Remediation deferred with criteria in signalman-4gp.4.

Recent changes (decision 0007, src/changes/): delivery tools POST /changes (bearer SIGNALMAN_CHANGES_TOKEN, secret env only; unset = routes absent) with {kind, summary, component?, at?, source?, url?}. Native adapters: POST /changes/argocd takes an Argo CD Application (or {app, context}) via bearer; POST /changes/gitlab takes GitLab webhooks with X-Gitlab-Token (same token, raw) and X-Gitlab-Event (Deployment success -> deploy, Feature Flag -> flag, Release create -> release, Merge Request merge -> merge; others 200 ignored). GitLab timestamps normalised to RFC 3339. ChangeLog is in-memory per replica (1000 newest); triage offers matches on component hints or platform-wide within flow.change_window_minutes (120). Fixtures under examples/changes/.

Configuration precedence (decision 0006, src/config.rs): built-in default < TOML file (--config, SIGNALMAN_CONFIG, ./signalman.toml, /etc/signalman/config.toml) < environment variable < flag. config.rs is the only module reading non-secret env vars; secrets (TYPESAFE_API_KEY, INCIDENTIO_API_KEY, INCIDENTIO_WEBHOOK_SECRET, BACKSTAGE_TOKEN) are env only and refused from the file. [policy], [triage.text], [[triage.teams]] are file-only. Every new setting: schema in Settings, resolve in Config::resolve, row in docs/configuration.md (tests/config_precedence.rs checks ENV_VARS appear in the doc).

GitHub Actions on this repository never ran: every job is refused at scheduling with the billing annotation ('recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased'). Check-run annotations are readable unauthenticated at api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo>/check-runs/<id>/annotations. Nothing in the repo fixes this; the account owner must fix Billing & plans, then re-run. Tracked as signalman-oqj.

Harness (signalman-o77): nine agents in .claude/agents. Read-only reviewers/auditors report, writers edit. config-reviewer = the seven places a setting lives (Settings schema, effective struct, resolve, ENV_VARS, unit test, docs/configuration.md row, example TOML / .env.example) plus decision 0006 rules; observability-reviewer = instrument names only in telemetry.rs, service.operation spans on every pub async client method, no bodies/secrets in span fields, docs table and tests/telemetry.rs agree; test-writer = wiremock per upstream, real TcpListener for transports, .expect(n) on writes, footguns (tuple-drop of MockServer, once-per-process globals, multi_thread for blocking exporters, up_to_n_times sequencing); pr-shepherd = PR body shape Summary / Decisions to review / Test plan, CI billing-block signature (runner_id 0, done within ~10 s of created_at, no steps, same on main) and the one standing-down comment; refactor-scout = pub items with no references outside their definition are dead because publish=false, plus duplicates/stale comments/unused deps, ranked by value over risk; docs-auditor = claims vs code with grep, why-gaps per section, links/anchors/last_reviewed/nav/index drift; docs-writer = problem first, then decision, rejected alternative, cost; link ADRs for the why. Hook llms-on-docs-edit.sh regenerates llms.txt after Edit/Write of docs/*.md, README.md, mkdocs.yml (silent when a page is not yet in the nav). Typical feature: test-writer + docs-writer in parallel with code, then config-reviewer + observability-reviewer on the diff, then pr-shepherd. Cleanup: refactor-scout + docs-auditor first.

incident.io contract: OpenAPI v3 at https://api.incident.io/v1/openapiV3.json (the /v1/openapi.json endpoint is removed, returns 410); guides at https://docs.incident.io/llms.txt; webhooks guide at https://docs.incident.io/api-reference/webhooks.md. Webhooks are Svix-signed (webhook-id/-timestamp/-signature, HMAC-SHA256 over id.ts.body, secret is base64 after whsec_). src/incidentio/webhook.rs is pinned to Svix's published test vector.

Laya (huggingface convaiinnovations/laya, Apache 2.0, pip laya, 421M ModernBERT-large) implements the System One wire shape (state + noul/choice/score questions -> answers with probabilities/confidence, extra 'rl_agent' key ignored by serde). signalman runs unchanged against a shim (examples/laya/serve_laya.py) via typesafe.base_url; TYPESAFE_API_KEY must be set but is ignored by the shim. Zero-shot on our alerts it is weak (every impact Major, owner confidence <0.5, 2-6 s/request on 4 CPUs); the model card says fine-tune first. Evaluation tracked in beads under signalman-ufg.

signalman mcp (src/mcp.rs, decision 0008): 5 always-on read-only MCP tools plus apply_qualification, registered only when mcp.allow_write is true (default off, 4gp.6). Two transports (4gp.7): stdio (rmcp transport-io) and Streamable HTTP (src/mcp/http.rs, rmcp transport-streamable-http-server, StreamableHttpService via axum route_service at /mcp). HTTP is stateless by construction: legacy_session_mode=false, json_response=true, NeverSessionManager; no Mcp-Session-Id, one POST = one JSON response, GET/DELETE 405, replicas need no affinity. Bearer token SIGNALMAN_MCP_TOKEN (McpToken newtype over changes::FeedToken; env-only; separate from the webhook secret and the feed token) checked by an axum from_fn_with_state layer in front of rmcp; 401 + WWW-Authenticate: Bearer. serve mounts /mcp on its own listener when mcp.enabled && token set (ignores mcp.transport/bind_address) with a Triager clone, so recent_changes shares the ChangeLog (Arc) - the only live-feed configuration. signalman mcp with transport=http is MCP-only on mcp.bind_address (required) + /healthz. mcp.allowed_hosts = rmcp Host/DNS-rebinding check; empty disables it on purpose (the token already defeats rebinding; rmcp default loopback-only breaks in k8s). Read tools wrap one Triager forced to DryRun; apply_qualification bypasses write_back, re-derives writes from the caller Outcome (validate/decision/answers/expected_tags), refuses alert_id mismatch; write_note replaces in place. Gotchas: Implementation::from_build_env() gives rmcp own name - use Implementation::new(env!(..)). #[tool_handler(router = self.tool_router)] needed when tools span several #[tool_router] blocks merged with +/+=. Unregistered tool => invalid_params "tool not found", not method_not_found. rmcp reqwest client: StreamableHttpClientTransportConfig.auth_header is the BARE token and the config is #[non_exhaustive] (mutate a Default). rmcp logs "Service initialized as server" at INFO per stateless request: RUST_LOG=rmcp=warn. Rust footgun: let (t, ..) = f().await drops unbound tuple fields (wiremock MockServer) at end of statement - bind to _names. Shell footgun: never put backticks inside a double-quoted bd remember/close string, bash runs them. Docs for agents (4gp.3): docs/llms.txt + llms-full.txt are generated by scripts/gen-llms-txt.sh from mkdocs.yml nav + frontmatter, drift-checked in mise docs:check/CI/prek; never hand-edit, run mise run docs:llms; a page opts out with llms: false (ADR template). Epic signalman-4gp planned scope is complete; 4gp.4 (remediation) stays deferred.

OpenTelemetry in signalman (m28.2, src/telemetry.rs, docs/observability.md). Crates: opentelemetry/opentelemetry_sdk/opentelemetry-otlp 0.32 with tracing-opentelemetry 0.33 - tracing-opentelemetry numbers releases ONE AHEAD of the opentelemetry crate it depends on (0.33 -> otel 0.32); cargo add of matching numbers fails to resolve. Features: otlp http-proto + reqwest-blocking-client (the SDK default: PeriodicReader and BatchSpanProcessor run on their own std thread and call the exporter with block_on, so the async reqwest client would panic without a runtime; the blocking client is built on a spawned thread inside the SDK); otlp reqwest is 0.13 like ours, no dual tree, no tonic. with_endpoint on the HTTP exporter is used AS-IS (only the env var path appends /v1/traces), so telemetry.rs appends /v1/traces and /v1/metrics itself; OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS is read by the exporter (env-only secret), per-signal endpoint/protocol vars are ignored by design. Providers::init installs registry + EnvFilter + fmt layer (+ otel layer and global meter provider when an endpoint is set); it must run once in main before any span, and Providers::shutdown must run at exit (main does it via spawn_blocking) or a one-shot CLI run exports nothing. Instruments are created lazily from the global meter via telemetry::metrics() (OnceLock) - fine because init precedes first use; in tests without a provider everything is a no-op. Spans: #[tracing::instrument] on client methods (service.operation names), triage/triage.flow on the Triager, webhook.receive per delivery, triage.background follows_from the request span (rendered as a span link). Upstream errors are counted in http::send_with_retries which now takes a service label. tests/telemetry.rs uses wiremock as the OTLP collector (protobuf keeps strings verbatim, so body_string contains checks work) with flavor=multi_thread and shutdown in spawn_blocking. Sandbox footgun: target/ grows past 20 GB across feature changes and the disk fills silently (rustc exits 101 with no diagnostic); rm -rf target/debug/incremental target/release target/doc frees ~4 GB, cargo clean frees all.

Project renamed from rustsafe to signalman on 2026-09-20 (crate, binary, CLI, env var SIGNALMAN_ADDR, docs, beads prefix). The GitHub repository must be renamed by the owner to chussenot/signalman; git redirects keep the old URL working.

Quality gates before any push: cargo fmt --all --check; RUSTFLAGS=-D warnings cargo clippy --all-targets (pedantic, unwrap_used); cargo test (no network: wiremock mocks both APIs); RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc --no-deps. Product names allowed in docs via clippy.toml doc-valid-idents.

Readiness (m28.3, src/readiness.rs): GET /readyz on the serve router, 200/503 with a JSON Report (ready, checked_at, cached, upstreams[{service, ok, latency_ms, error?}]) and Cache-Control: no-store. Checks are the cheapest authenticated calls: typesafe list_models, incidentio identity, backstage by-query limit 1 (only when a catalog is configured); concurrent via tokio::join, each under server.readiness_timeout_seconds (default 3), report cached server.readiness_cache_seconds (default 30, 0 = every request), failures cached too; a tokio Mutex around the cache serialises concurrent probes. The deadline includes the client retry policy, so a short deadline reports timed out rather than the transport error. Trade-off documented in docs/operations.md: an upstream outage marks every replica unready; incident.io retries for 24h so that is accepted. AppState::with_limits builds a default Probe; main replaces it with cfg.server.readiness(). Probe::new(&triager, settings) clones the three clients. Not mounted on the MCP-only HTTP process.

Receiver bounds (m28.1, src/serve.rs Limits): admission = max_concurrent + max_queued permits tried at delivery time BEFORE the webhook-id is marked seen; beyond it 503 + Retry-After: 30 so incident.io retries (up to 24h). running semaphore = max_concurrent. Each triage under tokio::time::timeout(server.triage_timeout_seconds); overrun -> Err outcome, tags already written stay. Defaults 8 / 64 / 60 s; config [server] keys + SIGNALMAN_MAX_CONCURRENT_TRIAGES / _MAX_QUEUED_TRIAGES / _TRIAGE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS.

Tsuga (observability, tsuga.com): no public API spec. GET https://api.tsuga.com/v0/open-api exists but needs an operation API key (401 otherwise). Web bundles evidence POST /v0/alerts/ongoing/query (filters owners, searchQuery, priorities, clusterIds, triggeredBy key:value, types monitor|slo). Decision 0005 (signalman-3l7.4): Tsuga alerts enter through Tsuga's native incident.io integration and are read back as related firing alerts; no Tsuga client until the spec is read (signalman-3l7.6).

TypeSafe docs are the API contract: start at https://docs.typesafe.ai/llms.txt; API reference at /api.md; append .md to any page path for markdown. No Rust SDK exists; src/client.rs mirrors the Python SDK defaults (jev-latest, 10s timeout, 2 retries 0.5s→5s, retry on 408/429/5xx, honour Retry-After).
